title: Hierarchical-priority queueing harness for mixed-workload batching effects
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: quantify how a hierarchical priority queueing layer interacts with continuous batching to affect tokens/sec and p95 latency across mixed workloads. We suspect that priority isolation (short low-cost chat requests vs long high-token completions) changes batching dynamics nonlinearly: tail amplification for low-priority classes and suppressed batch fill for high-priority classes. This ticket defines a harness, data collection plan, and regression detection criteria to measure those effects and propose mitigations.

Scope: synthetic and recorded-production traces; two-class workload mix (chatty <64 tokens, interactive completions 256-2048 tokens), three arrival patterns (Poisson, bursty superposition, and diurnal + diurnal spike), and two queueing policies: FIFO baseline and hierarchical-priority (strict priority + bandwidth reservation). Evaluate tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue occupancy distribution, batch size distribution, KV-cache hit impact, and throughput under backpressure.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Under mixed bursty arrivals, strict priority degrades p95 for the low-bandwidth class due to head-of-line blocking from batched long requests.
- H2: Bandwidth reservation (soft caps) improves tail for low-cost requests with minimal tokens/sec loss for high-cost requests.
- H3: Continuous batching tuned for average session length will mis-estimate batch windows for multi-modal length distributions, producing throughput regressions detectable via EWMA of tokens/sec and p95 drift.

Harness design summary:
- Traffic generator: rewritten load-gen (go) that can replay production trace CSVs and produce parameterized synthetic mixes. Supports session affinity, streaming tokens, and variable token production rates.
- Queue simulator: pluggable queue policy module (FIFO, strict-priority, weighted-reservations) that mirrors production routing layer API.
- Runtime shim: injects probes into serving runtime to capture batch boundary timestamps, per-batch model variant, inference duration (model execution), kernel selection tag, kv-cache hit/miss per request, and token emission counts.
- Metrics pipeline: Prom metrics + time-series export to Grafana/Prometheus and snapshot export to parquet for offline analysis. Additional per-experiment artifact: batch-size histogram (0..128+), per-class queue-length histogram, per-request annotation with arrival_time, service_start, service_end, tokens_emitted.
- Regression detection: dual approach: (1) online EWMA control chart on tokens/sec and p95 with configurable window and alpha; (2) offline statistical test (two-sample KS for latency distributions per class) comparing current run vs baseline run with multiple seeds. Alert if EWMA drift > 4% sustained 15m or p95 KS p-value < 0.01.

Planned experiments:
1) Baseline FIFO with default batching window (8ms adaptive) across mixes: 50/50, 80/20 short/long, 20/80. Measure tokens/sec and p95 for both classes.
2) Strict-priority preemptive: same mixes. Track starvation metrics for low-priority class.
3) Weighted-reservation (20% bandwidth to low class, 80% to high by token-cap) and reservation size sweep (10/20/30/40%).
4) Batching-window sweep: 4ms/8ms/16ms/32ms under each policy to find knee for throughput vs tail.
5) KV-cache warm vs cold scenarios to quantify batching interactions when cache miss causes long model execution.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Reproducible scripts that run full experiment matrix and produce artifact tarball.
- Baseline characterization: tokens/sec and p95 per class within expected bounds (documented).
- Clear mitigation recommendation (e.g., 20% reservation + 8ms adaptive) that improves low-class p95 by >=25% with tokens/sec loss <5% for high-class, or a documented trade-off if impossible.

Risks and assumptions:
- Synthetic mixes may not capture correlated session behavior seen in production (we will import 3 weeks of anonymized traces).
- Instrumentation overhead may change batching timing; we will measure probe overhead and subtract it from timing metrics.
- Tight coupling between kernel selection and latency could confound queueing effects; collect kernel tags to stratify results.

Deliverables:
- sources/benchmarks/hier-priority-experiments_{date}.parquet (artifact), Grafana dashboards, README with run instructions, and a PR with code changes to load-gen and queue-policy module.
